A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVGD convergence work. Their complete main texts, equations, conceptual diagram, references and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching proofs relocated in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports mathematical convergence results and proofs, including Appendix A, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V3 remains theoretical throughout its main text and Appendices A.1–A.6. Its additional discrete-time results are theorems and proofs, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The discrete and continuous SVGD updates remain the same, as do the bilinear-plus-translation-invariant and Matérn kernel constructions. V3's initialization and step-size conditions specify guarantees for the existing iteration; it does not introduce a new update or model component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical test scenarios. Examples of potentials, target distributions and kernels illustrate theoretical applicability rather than evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Comparisons with Shi and Mackey, population-limit SVGD and modified particle algorithms concern published theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, splits, preprocessing or evaluation budgets. V3's explicit step-size and iteration formulas are conditions of its new theorem, not settings of a reported experiment.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or case studies. The added energy-growth and Jacobian arguments are mathematical derivations assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3's additional probability bounds are theoretical guarantees rather than empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: There are no measured numerical results, empirical rankings or observed qualitative findings in either version. The additional convergence-rate results are formal theoretical contributions assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V3 adds discrete-time Assumption 2, Theorem 3 and Appendix A.3, with energy-growth and Jacobian bounds supporting explicit finite-step KSD rates. V1 only sketches discrete-time extendability. V3 also explicitly assumes existence and completeness of the continuous-time dynamics, strengthens initial-density regularity from C^1 to C^2 and several kernel conditions from C^2 to C^3, and corrects the Lyapunov derivative from average gradient of V to average V in the retained moment-bound proof.

C1.justification: V1's established main contributions concern continuous time, followed by a general assertion of discrete-time extendability. V3 makes a quantified discrete-time KSD guarantee a principal contribution. Its abstract changes the overall dimension-dependence claim from linear to polynomial while retaining the continuous-time linear bound, and explicitly confines the proved Wasserstein convergence to continuous time.

C2.justification: New Remarks 3–4 explain how tail growth, initial energy and a nonuniform Jacobian bound govern discretization error and step-size selection. Remark 6 adds a test-function explanation for Wasserstein's dimensional sensitivity. V3 also expressly defers discrete-time Wasserstein and propagation-of-chaos extensions, refining the scope of v1's broad extension discussion.

D1.justification: Where v1 only calls for sufficiently small steps, v3 Equation 10 specifies step-size dependence on particle count, dimension, tail-growth parameter and initial-energy threshold, together with an iteration count. Theorem 3 describes energy-restricted initialization. These are additional theoretical parameter prescriptions; neither version supplies implementation code, hardware or measured runtime.

R1.justification: V3 adds Barp et al. (2022), Gorham and Mackey (2015), Lambert et al. (2021), Brooks et al. (2011) and Raginsky et al. (2017), and removes Blei et al. (2017). It adds discussion distinguishing its discrete finite-particle analysis from population-limit bounds. The central positioning against Shi and Mackey (2024) remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized to present challenges and contributions before a separate past-work discussion. V3 separates continuous- and discrete-time sections and moves most retained proofs into a six-part appendix, while retaining Theorem 1's proof in the main text. Expanded notation, revised scope statements and explanatory remarks substantially change the document's organization.

P2.justification: V3 comprehensively changes the typesetting: the title and affiliation block is redesigned, centered small-cap section headings become larger left-aligned bold headings, running headers are removed, and equations and paragraphs are extensively reflowed. The existing convergence diagram moves from page 2 to page 4 with its conceptual content retained. No empirical figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: V1's discrete-time extension paragraph supplies no explicit finite-step bound or supporting proof. V3's Theorem 3 and Appendix A.3 provide quantified step-size and iteration requirements and detailed control of discretization error, substantially strengthening the connection to implemented SVGD. Explicit existence and regularity conditions also improve precision. The discrete-time guarantee remains restricted by tail-growth and initialization conditions, and Wasserstein/chaos extensions remain deferred, but these limits are now clearer.
